prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (or Concordia Venus).
what_it_adds: Salt as a wild resource, Forum tiles that give each player special powers, and two new maps (Byzantium and Hispania).
what_it_fixes: Gives the vine resource a real use (salt cities) and makes awkward storehouse turns more forgiving, so mistakes hurt less.
verdict_reason: Ranked the best all-round Concordia expansion by The Dice Drop, and the most-recommended pick in BGG buy-order threads; salt and two strong maps in one box.
notes: Salt is easy to add even with new players; BGG posters suggest holding off on Forum tiles until everyone knows the base game. Works with every map.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (or Concordia Venus).
what_it_adds: Double-sided map: Roma (with a ship track) and Sicilia (with production bonuses).
what_it_fixes: Fresh openings once the Italia/Imperium boards feel solved, and the Sicilia side makes low-count and solo games tighter.
verdict_reason: The Dice Drop calls the map packs essential and names Roma / Sicilia the standout first map, with Sicilia the preferred side.
notes: Newest map pack in the line; pairs well with Solitaria for solo play.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (or Concordia Venus).
what_it_adds: Double-sided map: Aegyptus (Nile flood food bonus, frankincense/gold trade for money and points) and Creta (tight 20-city map in nine provinces).
what_it_fixes: Base maps feel open at 2-3 players; Creta and Aegyptus give small groups a crowded, competitive board.
verdict_reason: BGG players single it out for 2-3 player groups: Creta is near-ideal for two and Aegyptus for two or three, with its own special rules.
notes: Playable at all counts, but the maps get very cut-throat at 4-5 players (publisher blurb).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game or Concordia Venus.
what_it_adds: Solo mode and 2-player co-op against an automated opponent (Contrarius) run by a card deck and dice; can also act as a third player in a 2-player game.
what_it_fixes: Concordia has no solo mode out of the box, and 2-player games can feel loose without a third presence on the board.
verdict_reason: Essential for solo players per The Dice Drop and BGG, but easy to skip for groups that never play alone; best paired with a map pack.
notes: Buy it first instead of Salsa if you mostly play solo.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the original Concordia base game.
what_it_adds: Fish market module (changes the Prefect action and the economy) plus a double-sided map: Balearica and Cyprus.
what_it_fixes: Adds a new economic module that works on every map, not just more geography.
verdict_reason: BGG regulars rate the fish market as an excellent module usable with all maps and expansions, and suggest getting it before Venus if you skip team play.
notes: Concordia Venus owners should buy Balearica & Italia instead; same fish market, but the back side is the Italia map the Venus box lacks.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the original Concordia base game.
what_it_adds: Team play (2v2, 3v3), a sixth player color, Venus god cards, and two maps (Hellas and the modular Ionium).
what_it_fixes: Lets 6 players play and adds a partnership mode; Ionium can be sized for 2-6 players.
verdict_reason: Rated worth it for team play or 6 players, but The Dice Drop and BGG posters say it is skippable if your group plays 3-5 without teams.
notes: Different product from the standalone Concordia Venus box (base game + Venus content). If you do not own Concordia yet, BGG posters suggest buying Concordia Venus standalone instead.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (or Concordia Venus).
what_it_adds: Double-sided map: Britannia and Germania; Germania has its own quirky special rules.
what_it_fixes: Adds new board layouts to change openings after many plays on Italia and Imperium.
verdict_reason: BGG players call Britannia / Germania a nice variant map pack; buy it once you want more map variety rather than as a first add-on.
notes: The first Concordia expansion. Amazon also lists it under ASIN B082SKXHFJ.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (or Concordia Venus).
what_it_adds: Double-sided map: the large Gallia board and the small Corsica board.
what_it_fixes: Gives both bigger and smaller groups another board to learn after the base maps.
verdict_reason: BGG advice is to pick map packs by the player counts you actually play; Gallia & Corsica is pure map variety with no new module.
notes: The Amazon listing found was the German edition (Erweiterung); buy the English Rio Grande edition from a US retailer.

prerequisite_rule: Needs Concordia Venus (standalone); also works with the original Concordia.
what_it_adds: Fish market module plus a double-sided map: Balearica and Italia.
what_it_fixes: Gives Concordia Venus owners the fish market and the classic Italia map, which the Venus box does not include.
verdict_reason: Same fish market BGG players praise in Balearica & Cyprus; only the right buy if you own the Concordia Venus standalone box.
notes: Original Concordia owners already have Italia, so they should buy Balearica & Cyprus instead.

what_it_adds: Sea animals that live in new aquarium enclosures built next to water, reef-dweller chain abilities, a fourth university, 20 alternate action cards (swap in 2 at setup), new sponsors, conservation projects, bonus tiles and final scoring cards, plus shaped wooden track markers.
what_it_fixes: Base-game card rows can clog with cards nobody wants; wave icons on sea cards flush the display, and the alternate action cards make each player's engine feel different.
verdict_reason: Won the 2023 Golden Geek Best Expansion award and is rated 8.9 on BGG; reviewers single out the alternate action cards and faster card-row churn as the reason it improves the base game.
notes: Includes replacement copies of some base-game cards with corrections. Adds 119 cards, so sleeve buyers need extra sleeves. Fits inside the base-game box.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game. Works with or without Marine Worlds.
what_it_adds: Five new zoo-map layouts: four double-sided boards with the Tournament 1 map on one side (so all 4 players can share it) and Artificial Intelligence, Caves, Drawing Board and Lagoon on the other, with a reference sheet for the new map abilities.
what_it_fixes: Gives experienced players fresh opening puzzles once the 8 base-game maps feel solved, and adds a shared map so everyone starts on equal footing.
verdict_reason: Cheap way to add variety (5 maps for about $13) and rated 8.6 on BGG; Feuerland confirmed on BGG it does not require Marine Worlds.
notes: Includes the 2024 World Series of Board Gaming tournament map. Some map icons come from Marine Worlds, but the included rules sheet explains them.

what_it_adds: Two identical double-sided zoo maps: Map 9 Geographical Zoo (continent areas give a one-time bonus when you house a matching animal there) and Map 10 Rescue Station (dig bonuses let you tuck discarded animals under your map so their icons count).
what_it_fixes: Adds two new map puzzles for groups that have played the base maps many times.
verdict_reason: Only two new layouts and a lower BGG rating (8.2) than Map Pack 2, so it's best for players who want every map once they own the other expansions.
notes: Contains two copies of the same double-sided board (Maps 9 and 10), so two players can use the same map.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Twilight Imperium Fourth Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Seven new factions, faction mechs, three leaders per faction (agent, commander, hero), exploration decks with relics, 40 new system and hyperlane tiles, legendary planets, and two extra player colors for up to 8 players.
what_it_fixes: Base-game factions can feel thin and the map static; exploration, leaders and mechs give every faction more to do, and 7–8 player games become possible.
verdict_reason: Regular TI4 groups treat it as the default way to play: one BGG regular calls it "clean and elegant" next to Thunder's Edge, and another says they would never play the base game without it. It is all-or-nothing, so groups who find base TI4 heavy enough may skip it.
notes: Played all-in: you use all of its rules together rather than picking modules. Adds the two player colors needed for 7–8 players.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Twilight Imperium Fourth Edition base game; works with or without Prophecy of Kings.
what_it_adds: Five new factions, a breakthrough card for every faction, the Thunder's Edge expedition and legendary planet, the Fracture with neutral units and relics, 20 optional galactic event cards, the printed Twilight Codex content including the Council Keleres faction, new faction reference cards, and the Twilight's Fall alternate game mode.
what_it_fixes: Breakthroughs buff weaker factions, galactic events let groups vary each game, and players who never printed the free Codex PDFs get that content in the box.
verdict_reason: BGG regulars like that it is modular (use as much or as little as you want) but warn that it adds overlapping rules and is wilder than Prophecy of Kings; buy it after Prophecy of Kings if your group wants more variety.
notes: Built to work with the base game alone; Prophecy of Kings-specific parts (mechs, leaders) are simply left out if you don't own it. Seven- and eight-player games still need Prophecy of Kings' extra colors. Also includes six faction cards for the spin-off Twilight Inscription.
